title: Frankenstein; or, the modern prometheus
author: Mary Wollstonecraft Shelley
reader_preference: favor eerie creation scenes, lonely landscapes, and tense encounters between Victor and the Creature over quieter dialogue

scout.cultural_context: Early 19th-century Romantic-era Britain and continental Europe
scout.suggested_style: dark Romantic oil painting, Caspar David Friedrich–inspired Gothic atmosphere, moonlit alpine landscapes and candlelit laboratories, deep indigo and umber palette with sickly green highlights, dramatic chiaroscuro, textured brushstrokes, mist and storm light
scout.suggested_reader_preference: favor eerie creation scenes, lonely landscapes, and tense encounters between Victor and the Creature over quieter dialogue
scout.rationale: Shelley’s novel blends Gothic horror with Romantic-era fascination with nature and sublime landscapes; a dark Romantic oil style echoes that period and mood. The story offers many visually striking moments—creation, Arctic pursuit, alpine meetings—supporting roughly one illustration per chapter.

poster.description:
Obsessed with the secrets of life, young Swiss scientist Victor Frankenstein pushes beyond the boundaries of natural philosophy—and pays a terrible price. At the University of Ingolstadt he pursues a forbidden breakthrough, scavenging from charnel-houses and dissecting rooms until he discovers how to animate lifeless matter. But when the towering being he assembles finally opens its dull yellow eye, Victor is seized not with triumph but with horror. He abandons the creature to the world, setting in motion a chain of suffering neither creator nor creation can escape.

Left alone, the nameless being struggles to understand humanity from the shadows, learning language, kindness, and hope by secretly observing a rural family. Yet every attempt to approach the human world ends in terror and violence. Rejected by all and tormented by loneliness, the Creature turns to the one person responsible for his existence: Victor himself. What begins as a plea for compassion becomes a vow of vengeance.

From candlelit laboratories and storm-lashed mountains to desolate islands and the frozen wastes of the Arctic, Mary Shelley’s haunting tale unfolds as a warning about ambition without responsibility. Through the intertwined voices of explorer Robert Walton, the haunted Victor, and the eloquent Creature, the novel explores the dangerous hunger for glory, the loneliness of the outsider, and the moral burden of creation.

Dark, tragic, and strangely tender, Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus remains one of literature’s most powerful meditations on what it means to make life—and what it means to be human.
poster.cover_scene: A moonlit Alpine landscape where a lone figure stands on a crag while a towering shadowed creature emerges from storm clouds above distant laboratories and icy seas, evoking ambition, creation, and pursuit across Europe and the Arctic.
